one_line: Last major Sultan of independent Bengal, ruling Gaur amid Mughal and Afghan pressures in the mid-16th century.

appearance.age_look: mid-40s, average build with a slight dignity-bearing weight
appearance.face: oval face, wheatish-brown Bengali complexion, neatly trimmed black beard with a few streaks of grey, sharp nose, thoughtful almond eyes under slightly arched brows, default expression calm and calculating with a hint of concern
appearance.hair: black hair kept short and tidy beneath a deep green, slightly conical quilted Muslim cap with a narrow gold band at the base
appearance.costume: over a long-sleeved, ankle-length off‑white cotton jama tied on the right, he wears a rich deep green silk jama-coat with side slits and subtle gold floral brocade, fastened with three small gold toggles at the chest; a wide maroon silk patka sash wraps his waist and knots slightly off-center with one decorated end hanging to mid‑thigh, embroidered with fine repeating gold vine motifs; loose cream churidar-style trousers bunch neatly at the ankles, meeting soft brown leather mojari shoes with curved but modest toes; over his shoulders rests a light, pale gold cotton shawl with a thin green border, draped symmetrically to suggest royal formality without excess bulk.
appearance.signature: a slightly curved Indo-Persian talwar with a simple steel hilt and small disc pommel, sheathed in a dark brown leather scabbard with two narrow brass bands, hanging from a practical brown belt over his maroon sash at his left hip, his right hand often resting lightly on the hilt

ref_desc: Nasiruddin Nasrat Shah is a mid-40s Bengali sultan with an oval wheatish face and trimmed greying beard, wearing a deep green silk jama-coat over off-white garments, maroon sash, cream churidar, brown mojari, green cap, and carrying a sheathed talwar on a brown belt.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model sheet of Nasiruddin Nasrat Shah: a mid-40s Bengali sultan with an oval wheatish-brown face, thoughtful almond eyes and a neatly trimmed black beard streaked with grey, wearing a deep green silk jama-coat with subtle gold floral brocade over a long off-white cotton jama, fastened by three small gold toggles at the chest. Wrap his waist with a wide maroon silk patka sash, embroidered at the hanging end with fine repeating gold vine motifs, over cream churidar-style trousers that gather at the ankles and brown leather mojari shoes with modestly curved toes. Place a pale gold cotton shawl with a thin green border over his shoulders, draped symmetrically, and show his black hair mostly hidden under a deep green slightly conical quilted cap with a narrow gold band at the base. At his left hip, hang a slightly curved talwar in a dark brown leather scabbard with two brass bands from a practical brown belt worn over the sash, his right hand resting lightly on the hilt. Use deep green, maroon, off-white, pale gold, and brown as the dominant colours and present him front-facing, side, and back to clearly show face, hair, garments, and weapon.
